name: vcard-ical
label: vCard 4.0 + iCal
description: RFC standards for contacts and calendar data — interoperable with every phone/email client

table_notes.vcard_contact: Core contact record per RFC 6350 vCard 4.0 — one row per person or organization, with structured name components and JSONB fields for multi-value properties.
table_notes.vcard_email: Multi-valued EMAIL property for a contact; each row is one address with RFC-defined type tags (work, home, etc.) and a preference rank.
table_notes.vcard_phone: Multi-valued TEL property for a contact; each row is one phone number with type tags and preference rank per RFC 6350 §6.4.1.
table_notes.ical_calendar: Top-level VCALENDAR container per RFC 5545 — one row per calendar feed, grouping events under an owner and timezone.
table_notes.ical_event: Individual VEVENT records per RFC 5545 — stores timing, recurrence, attendees, and geolocation for a single event instance or recurring series.

vcard_contact.name: id
vcard_contact.description: Internal surrogate primary key for the contact row

vcard_contact.name: uid
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 UID property — globally unique identifier used for CardDAV sync and import/export

vcard_contact.name: fn
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 FN (formatted name) — the display name as a single pre-formatted string

vcard_contact.name: family_name
vcard_contact.description: Surname / last name component of the vCard N property

vcard_contact.name: given_name
vcard_contact.description: First / given name component of the vCard N property

vcard_contact.name: additional_name
vcard_contact.description: Middle name(s) or additional name component of the vCard N property

vcard_contact.name: honorific_prefix
vcard_contact.description: Honorific prefix (e.g. Dr., Prof., Mr.) from the vCard N property

vcard_contact.name: honorific_suffix
vcard_contact.description: Honorific suffix (e.g. Jr., III, MD) from the vCard N property

vcard_contact.name: nickname
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 NICKNAME property — array of nickname strings, e.g. ["Jim", "Jimmy"]

vcard_contact.name: photo_url
vcard_contact.description: URL of the contact's photo (RFC 6350 PHOTO as URI value)

vcard_contact.name: birthday
vcard_contact.description: Contact's date of birth (RFC 6350 BDAY property)

vcard_contact.name: anniversary
vcard_contact.description: Contact's wedding or relationship anniversary (RFC 6350 ANNIVERSARY property)

vcard_contact.name: gender
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 GENDER sex component: M=male, F=female, O=other, N=none, U=unknown

vcard_contact.name: org
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 ORG property — array of org unit strings, e.g. ["Acme Corp", "Engineering"]

vcard_contact.name: title
vcard_contact.description: Job title within the organization (RFC 6350 TITLE property)

vcard_contact.name: party_role
vcard_contact.description: Functional role or occupation description (RFC 6350 ROLE property)

vcard_contact.name: url
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 URL property — JSONB array of {value, type} objects, one per web address

vcard_contact.name: note
vcard_contact.description: Free-text note or comment about the contact (RFC 6350 NOTE property)

vcard_contact.name: categories
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 CATEGORIES property — array of keyword strings used for grouping/tagging contacts

vcard_contact.name: rev
vcard_contact.description: RFC 6350 REV property — timestamp of the last revision of the vCard record

vcard_contact.name: created_at
vcard_contact.description: Row insertion timestamp (database-managed, not part of the vCard spec)

vcard_email.name: contact_id
vcard_email.description: Foreign key to vcard_contact — the contact that owns this email address

vcard_email.name: address
vcard_email.description: The email address string (max 320 chars per RFC 5321)

vcard_email.name: types
vcard_email.description: RFC 6350 type parameter array for this address, e.g. ["work", "internet"] or ["home"]

vcard_email.name: preference
vcard_email.description: RFC 6350 PREF parameter — 1 (most preferred) to 100 (least preferred); lower wins

vcard_email.name: label
vcard_email.description: Optional human-readable display label for this email entry (e.g. "Work", "Personal")

vcard_phone.name: contact_id
vcard_phone.description: Foreign key to vcard_contact — the contact that owns this phone number

vcard_phone.name: number
vcard_phone.description: Phone number string in E.164 or local format (RFC 6350 TEL value)

vcard_phone.name: types
vcard_phone.description: RFC 6350 type parameter array, e.g. ["cell", "voice"] or ["work", "fax"]

vcard_phone.name: preference
vcard_phone.description: RFC 6350 PREF parameter — 1 (most preferred) to 100 (least preferred); lower wins

ical_calendar.name: id
ical_calendar.description: Internal surrogate primary key for the calendar

ical_calendar.name: name
ical_calendar.description: Human-readable display name of the calendar (iCal X-WR-CALNAME)

ical_calendar.name: description
ical_calendar.description: Free-text description of the calendar's purpose (iCal X-WR-CALDESC)

ical_calendar.name: color
ical_calendar.description: Display color for calendar UI (CSS hex or named color, iCal X-APPLE-CALENDAR-COLOR)

ical_calendar.name: timezone
ical_calendar.description: Default IANA timezone for events in this calendar (iCal X-WR-TIMEZONE)

ical_calendar.name: owner_uid
ical_calendar.description: Identifier of the user or account that owns this calendar (application-defined UID)

ical_calendar.name: prodid
ical_calendar.description: RFC 5545 PRODID — software product identifier that created this calendar feed

ical_event.name: id
ical_event.description: Internal surrogate primary key for the event row

ical_event.name: calendar_id
ical_event.description: Foreign key to ical_calendar — the calendar this event belongs to

ical_event.name: uid
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 UID property — globally unique event identifier used for CalDAV sync and deduplication

ical_event.name: summary
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 SUMMARY — short one-line title/subject of the event (shown in calendar grid)

ical_event.name: description
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 DESCRIPTION — detailed notes or body text for the event

ical_event.name: location
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 LOCATION — venue name or address string for the event

ical_event.name: geo_point
ical_event.description: PostGIS point derived from RFC 5545 GEO property (lat;long). Enables ST_DWithin proximity queries.

ical_event.name: dtstart
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 DTSTART — event start date/time in UTC (all-day events store midnight UTC)

ical_event.name: dtend
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 DTEND — event end date/time in UTC (exclusive end per RFC 5545 §3.8.2.2)

ical_event.name: all_day
ical_event.description: True when DTSTART/DTEND are DATE values (no time component) — renders as all-day in UIs

ical_event.name: rrule
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 RRULE string defining recurrence (e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=10)

ical_event.name: status
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 STATUS: TENTATIVE, CONFIRMED, or CANCELLED for events

ical_event.name: transp
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 TRANSP: OPAQUE (blocks time in free/busy) or TRANSPARENT (does not block)

ical_event.name: organizer
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 ORGANIZER cal-address (mailto: URI) of the person who created the event

ical_event.name: attendees
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 ATTENDEE list — array of {cn, email, partstat, role} objects per invitee

ical_event.name: categories
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 CATEGORIES — array of keyword strings for tagging and filtering events

ical_event.name: created_at
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 CREATED — timestamp when the event was first added to the calendar store

ical_event.name: last_modified
ical_event.description: RFC 5545 LAST-MODIFIED — timestamp of the most recent change to this event

short_description: RFC standards for contacts and calendar data — interoperable with every phone/email client
long_description: vCard 4.0 (RFC 6350) and iCalendar (RFC 5545) are the IETF standards for contacts and calendar data interchange, supported natively by every phone, email client, and calendar application. The schema covers the complete vCard data model with typed email/phone fields, iCalendar event records with RRULE recurrence, attendees, and geolocation.
when_to_use: Use for CRM systems, address book applications, scheduling/booking platforms, calendar sharing tools, or any application that needs to import/export contacts and events. vCard/iCal support is required for CalDAV/CardDAV server compatibility (used by iOS, Android, Thunderbird, Outlook). Essential for multi-platform calendar sync and contact migration tools.
